newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Banco Santander buys Banco de Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Banco Santander buys Banco de Venezuela.

text.p: Leading Spanish bank Banco Santander SA bought Venezuela's second largest bank Banco de Venezuela for $301.1 million at auction on Thursday, Fogade president Esther de Margulis said.

Santander bought 40 million shares, or 80 percent of Banco de Venezuela, Margulis said at the public presentation of the bidding results. Banco Bilbao Vizcaya SA, which was also registered for the auction, presented a blank bid.
Santander's bid topped the $228.8 million base price asked for the 80 percent share in Banco de Venezula.
"Santander has made it possible for us to realize our dreams," Margulis said. An earlier attempt to sell the bank collapsed in August after investors retired in confusion over the bidding process.

"We're delighted with the results, very proud ... the sale will help consolidate the opening of Venezuela's financial system," the head of Santander's Latin American banking operations Miguel Goguikian said.
"Our intention is to introduce new technology, new products, provide consumer choice ... to make Banco de Venezuela the market leader," he said.

The sale draws to a close a chapter in Venezuela's financial crisis which absorbed an estimated $11 billion in state bail-outs when the banking system tanked in 1994-5. Banco de Venezuela was taken over by Fogade in 1994.
Santander's entry is also expected to shake up the banking sector, forcing modernization and greater efficiency on other banks. "Competition is always good," Goguikian said.
Margulis said the bank's sale would bring in a total of $376.38 million, after including proceeds from a public offering designed to sweeten the sale and quell opposition.
Although 20 percent had been offered, small investors placed orders for just over half that -- some 10.28 percent of the bank worth 13.8 billion bolivars ($29.4 million).
Margulis said Santander would buy the bank's remaining shares. "Santander will have at least 90 percent of the bank," she said.
